title: Hypertrophic Discoid Lupus Preceding the Diagnosis of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus With Active Lupus Nephritis: A Case Report.
abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a systemic autoimmune disease with heterogeneous cutaneous and visceral manifestations. We report the case of a 26-year-old Japanese woman with SLE who initially presented with a diffuse eruption resembling Kaposi varicelliform eruption and was subsequently found to have severe organ involvement, including active lupus nephritis. The patient had a history of atopic dermatitis, and the eruption was initially treated as Kaposi varicelliform eruption; however, the lesions continued to worsen. The subsequent development of arthralgia, alopecia, and fatigue prompted further investigation, which revealed elevated anti-DNA antibody levels, hypocomplementemia, and newly detected proteinuria. Renal biopsy confirmed active lupus nephritis. Re-evaluation of the cutaneous lesions and the skin biopsy revealed marked hyperkeratosis, epidermal thickening, elongated rete ridges, basal vacuolar degeneration, and lymphocytic infiltration, while direct immunofluorescence demonstrated granular IgA and IgM deposition along dermal vessels. These clinicopathological findings, together with the newly established diagnosis of SLE, supported the diagnosis of hypertrophic lupus, the hypertrophic variant of discoid lupus. Treatment with glucocorticoids, mycophenolate mofetil, voclosporin, and hydroxychloroquine led to remission of the systemic manifestations, including lupus nephritis, with parallel improvement of the skin lesions. This case illustrates that the hypertrophic variant of discoid lupus can mimic other dermatological disorders and delay recognition of systemic disease. Careful assessment of extracutaneous findings is therefore important when evaluating atypical or treatment-refractory skin lesions.

title: Pregnancy in undifferentiated connective tissue disease: maternal disease course and outcomes in the prospective multicentre P-RHEUM.it study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate disease course, management, and outcomes in a prospective nationwide cohort of pregnant women with Undifferentiated Connective Tissue Disease (UCTD), identifying independent predictors of flares and adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs).
METHODS: The prospective multicentre P-RHEUM.it study enrolled pregnant UCTD patients before the 20th gestational week across 19 Italian tertiary centres (2018-2023). Baseline variables were assessed as predictors for maternal flares and APOs (primary outcomes), using confounder-adjusted multivariate Cox regression.
RESULTS: Among 175 pregnancies (173 women), 60.7% received hydroxychloroquine, 14.5% glucocorticoids, 3.5% immunosuppressants, and 45.1% low-dose aspirin (plus heparin in 9.8%). Mild flares occurred in 13.1% of pregnancies, mainly during the second trimester. APOs were recorded in 25.7% of pregnancies, mostly during the third trimester. The live birth rate was 95.7%, with 14.8% being preterm births (PTB). Flares were predicted by smoking (HR 5.3; 95%CI 1.8-15.6), anti-SSB/La positivity (HR 4.6; 95%CI 1.5-14.3), and non-Caucasian ethnicity (HR 4.4; 95%CI 1.6-11.9), while previous PTB (HR 3.4; 95%CI 1.2-9.7), mucocutaneous involvement (HR 2.2; 95%CI 1.1-4.7), and low complement (HR 2.2; 95%CI 1.1-4.7) predicted APOs. Flares and APOs occurred concomitantly in 3.4% of pregnancies.
CONCLUSIONS: APOs occurred in one-fourth of pregnancies and were predicted by mucocutaneous involvement and low complement levels at baseline, which are features that generally do not lead to intensified immunomodulatory and/or preventative treatment. Therefore, our data suggest that preconception risk stratification should aim at incorporating additional characteristics that can help better individualize the treatment before and during pregnancy.

title: Ex Vivo Immunomodulation of Blood from AML Patients at Relapse After Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation Improves Antileukemic Reactions Independent of Checkpoint Expression Profiles of T Cells and Blasts.
abstract: Background: Among other immune escape mechanisms, unfavorable expression patterns of inhibitory checkpoint molecules (ICMs) and their ligands (ICMLs) in T cells and blasts are known to play a major role in the relapse of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) post allogenic stem cell transplantation (SCT). Treatment options for AML patients at relapse are limited. Leukemia-derived dendritic cells (DCleu), generated with granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) and prostaglandin-E1 (PGE-1) ("Kit M"), mediate antileukemic immune responses after T cell-enriched mixed lymphocyte culture (MLC) with patient-derived immune cells. These effects have not yet been investigated in the context of ICM or ICML expression at AML relapse post SCT. Methods: We quantified the frequencies of uncultured ICM- and ICML-expressing T cells and blasts in peripheral blood (PB) samples from relapsed AML patients after SCT via flow cytometry. According to CD152+ expression in T cells and CD86+ in blasts, patients were categorized into three groups: (1) >20% CD152+ T cells and >20% CD86+ blasts, (2) >20% CD152+ T cells and ≤20% CD86+ blasts, and (3) <20% CD152+ T cells and ≤20% CD86+ blasts. DCs and DCleu were generated from patient samples using Kit M, followed by MLC and assessment of antileukemic activation using cytotoxicity assays. Additionally, detailed MLC analyses were performed in three selected cases presenting with CD86+ blasts. In one case, additional MLCs were performed using T cells from the patient's haploidentical parents, who showed markedly different CD152+ expression profiles. Results: The uncultured PB samples from 13 AML patients at relapse post SCT revealed high mean frequencies of CD152+- and CD279+-expressing T cells (48.0% CD152+ T cells [range: 2.1-83.7%]; 43.1% CD279+ T cells [range: 5.7-75.8%]) and CD86+ leukemic blasts (35.8% [range: 2.2-97.2%]). Ex vivo Kit M treatment induced DCleu and increased blast lysis after MLC compared with the untreated controls across all evaluable patients and ICM- and ICML-defined groups. A trend toward greater improvement in blast lysis was observed in patients with lower frequencies of CD152+ T cells and CD86+ blasts (<20%). Conclusions: Kit M increases ex vivo antileukemic immune responses in AML relapse after SCT, despite heterogeneous ICM and ICML expression patterns for T cells and leukemic blasts. These findings support further investigation of DCleu-based immunomodulation in the post-transplant relapse setting. In addition, donor-specific ICM expression profiles may warrant further evaluation as a potential factor in stem cell donor selection.
